audits.title: Sedation in a radiology department--do radiologists follow their own guidelines?
audits.standard: Royal College of Radiologists 2003 sedation guidelines
audits.setting: Department of Clinical Radiology, Ninewells Hospital, Dundee

cycle1.result: Low awareness of guidelines and variable practice on fasting and drug order.

cycle2.result: Some improvements; persisting deviation on fasting and giving opiate before benzodiazepine; trend towards shorter acting benzodiazepines.

audits.other_findings: Monitoring of vital signs was generally well done.
audits.citation: Eason D, Chakraverty S, Wildsmith JA. Sedation in a radiology department--do radiologists follow their own guidelines?. Scott Med J. 2011;56(2):61-63. doi:10.1258/smj.2010.010013. PMID: 21670128.

audits.title: Sedation Rate Reduction in Paediatric Renal Nuclear Medicine Examinations: Consequences of a Targeted Audit.
audits.setting: Paediatric urology and nuclear medicine department, Hospital of the Sisters of Charity, Linz

cycle1.result: Sedation rate 27.1%; 86% (60/70) would repeat the investigation under identical conditions; 77% (17/22) of patients over 5 felt good.

audits.intervention: Revised sedation policy with clear age limits, individual indication, staff education and optimised sedatives
audits.citation: Gernhold C, Kundtner N, Steinmair M, Henkel M, Oswald J, Haid B. Sedation Rate Reduction in Paediatric Renal Nuclear Medicine Examinations: Consequences of a Targeted Audit. Children (Basel). 2021;8(5):424. doi:10.3390/children8050424. PMID: 34065386.

audits.title: Retrospective audit of midazolam dose and intravenous sedation record keeping in a primary care oral surgery service.
audits.standard: IACSD standards for conscious sedation in dentistry
audits.setting: Primary care oral surgery service, Cheshire and Merseyside

cycle1.result: Missing elements in sedation record keeping identified (no figures given); midazolam within recommended dose range

cycle2.result: All clinicians aware of missing elements and able to complete accurate contemporaneous sedation records (no figures given)

audits.other_findings: No patient safety concerns or complications recorded.
audits.citation: Liew J, Winston M. Retrospective audit of midazolam dose and intravenous sedation record keeping in a primary care oral surgery service. Prim Dent J. 2022;11(1):50-57. doi:10.1177/20501684221085846. PMID: 35383494.

audits.title: EEG bispectral index sensor guidance improves accuracy and safety of procedural sedation.
audits.standard: 14 standards from the revised departmental sedation protocol based on national guidelines; BIS target 80-85
audits.setting: Interventional radiology, The Christie NHS Foundation Trust (fluoroscopic and combined endoscopic procedures)

cycle1.result: Re-audit: three sedation standards missed; 84% had light or moderate sedation (BIS 70-89); no reversal, airway management or hypoxaemia

audits.intervention: Revised sedation protocol with BIS-guided nurse titration of sedo-analgesia
audits.other_findings: Only the re-audit data are reported; mean midazolam 3.99 mg and fentanyl 92.3 μg.
audits.citation: Oh A, Karim N, Pitt A, Hodgetts S, Edwards DW, Mullan D, et al.. EEG bispectral index sensor guidance improves accuracy and safety of procedural sedation. Clin Radiol. 2024;79(12):e1490-e1496. doi:10.1016/j.crad.2024.08.033. PMID: 39317529.

audits.title: Assessment of the practice of pediatrics procedural sedation and analgesia for magnetic resonance imaging and computed tomography scan at a teaching hospital, Ethiopia, 2020: A clinical audit.
audits.standard: 20 standards from procedural sedation practice guidelines for MRI and CT
audits.setting: Imaging sites, University of Gondar teaching referral hospital

cycle1.result: 6 of 20 standards had 100% compliance, 3 had 0% and 11 were between 0 and 100%.

audits.other_findings: Staff were advised to adopt standards or local protocols.
audits.citation: Melesse DY, Mekonnen ZA, Kassahun HG, Workie MM, Filatie TD. Assessment of the practice of pediatrics procedural sedation and analgesia for magnetic resonance imaging and computed tomography scan at a teaching hospital, Ethiopia, 2020: A clinical audit. J Med Imaging Radiat Sci. 2021;52(2):272-276. doi:10.1016/j.jmir.2021.01.004. PMID: 33541790.
